scope: Released-SDK baseline for the WW34 consecutive-starts strip chart.
supported: set_hyper_connection(tables=..., relationships=...) for the two-table logical relationship (offense_franchise_id = franchise_id)
add_calculated_field(table_calc='Rows') for LOOKUP, PREVIOUS_VALUE, WINDOW_MAX and INDEX formulas
configure_chart(table_calc_overrides=...) writing ordering-field addressing plus nested table-calc dependency metadata
configure_layered_chart(axis_shelf='columns') for the nested Rows shelf Team / (Current * Consecutive) and mark_sizing for 1-axis-unit right-aligned bars
configure_worksheet_style(axis_style=..., header_formats=..., gridline_style=...) for the hidden streak axis, the index axis title and the row-header widths
add_dashboard with floating absolute zones at the author's geometry

findings.summary: set_hyper_connection inspects integer columns without id/code/zip in the name as measures, and a bare 'Week' field is bound as MONTH(Week) by the date-name heuristic, so raw season/week cannot be used as the discrete Rows/Detail pills the article asks for.
findings.workaround: Re-expose Season, Week and Player Id (plus a continuous Week Number for the in-range filter) as explicit discrete calculated fields; the article performs the same 'change to discrete' step in the UI.

findings.summary: configure_chart nests measures with '*' and dimensions with '/', so the Rows shelf came out as Team * (Current * Consecutive) instead of the author's Team / (Current * Consecutive).
findings.workaround: Use configure_layered_chart with axis_shelf='columns' so the index owns the continuous axis and Rows is built by the dimension shelf.
